utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order was conveyed to them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not my question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and that's why the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is: Who gave the order; not: Who was the messenger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that piece of information. I only recognise the format of the document and the situation it describes. I know that such documents are drafted as a rule when conveying someone's order, an order of a superior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you say that within -- or do you say that within the MUP in Belgrade we would see examples of official notes which do not disclose who is making the order, but only disclose the recipient of the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I am saying that in my career I received - I can give you an example - I received information from the chief of administration that he was conveying orders of the minister. However, since I have no information in relation to this document, the only thing I can do is to say that I recognise the format of it and I put it in that category.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will try to press you even further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Be my guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who could have issued the order conveyed to the chiefs of SUP by Sreten Lukic, that is to say to all SUP chiefs in K and M?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Since chiefs of SUPs are senior superiors, if we were to put Sreten Lukic before them as the person conveying the order, it could have been issued to him either by the minister or the chief of sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're quite clear that Lukic was the superior of the SUP chiefs?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He didn't say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, the transcript reads -- well, just repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Given that chiefs of SUPs are senior officials and that we have Sreten Lukic's name appearing here as conveying the information, it means that he did the same -- the very thing. The orders could have been issued by the minister or the chief of sector, that's what I had in mind. According to our system, chiefs of SUPs are answerable to the chief of the sector and the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we kindly ask the tape to be reviewed. I'm sure that the witness didn't say what was recorded the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's only right that we should ask CLSS to revise the interpretation at page 44, lines 24 and 25 -- in fact, 24 to 26 -- sorry, 24 and 25 and 45, line 1. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... from the record. I mentioned the name. Can the line -- page 59, line 24 -- 23, can it be deleted from the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're talking about page 45, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The reference I've just given for review by CLSS is inaccurate, but that's because my own transcript in front of me reverted to page 1 after 15 pages today. So, Mr. Lukic, to clarify that could you give me, first of all, the page reference and line reference for the correction or the review of the tape that you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's at page -- it's the same with Mr. Ivetic's transcript -- I have completely different numbers but I cannot review them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The only one that seems to have that is the middle computer which is not controlled by us. The one I have also has that we're on page 46 or 47 right now. So the reference I would give would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm on the same page as Mr. Ivetic and yourself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's hope that that can be accurately identified and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any event --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- the part that you mentioned will be redacted, Mr. Lukic, so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D778 brought up in e-court. We have the document in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe you can see it. Who sent this document, can you tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: In the signature block it says the head of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is what is typed, but we don't see the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, this is a type of dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the date of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: 15th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please read out the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: "Even though an order was issued on the 5th of April, 1999," citing someone's order, "to prevent civilians from leaving their place of residence and to guarantee for their safety and to take measures to protect the population. It has come to our attention that some of the said commanders --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Not commanders, officers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] " -- have not been obeying the order and they have been tolerating massive scales of departures of civilian population."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next I have to show you P1989 in order to compare the two -- in order to compare the dates. I know you did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the date concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It says here the 4th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the meeting was there your SUP chief while you were in Pristina, is that in relation to this date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: If the minutes contain the contents of the previous document then it is probably that meeting. Let me check. Yes, the problem of the moving out of Muslims and Turks is mentioned and that should be the meeting, yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first document, 6D666 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- the date is the 3rd of April, 1999. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The second document, reference is made to a document of the 5th of April, 1999. I have to ask you a direct question. Would you allow for a possibility that on the first document, this being 6D666, the date should have been the 5th of April instead of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, that calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm aware of that. I don't know how to proceed without directing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your view, in these two documents do we have the same task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: In terms of content they coincide sufficiently to accept your statement from my point of view after reviewing both documents. It is possible that a mistake was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, how does the 4th of April fit into all of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That the information could not be conveyed further before the 4th of April, and that actually on the first document, 6D666, we have typo mistake, it should be the 5th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you say light is shed on that by -- sorry, by P1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, how does it shed light on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that he learned about the information on that day, and that information if conveyed on the 4th could be -- the first document could be composed only the day later, not the day before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask you to have a look at P1996. We will also have three interconnected documents. Here we have minutes of a meeting held in the MUP staff for Kosovo and Metohija in Pristina on the 7th of May, 1999. I would kindly ask you to go to page 8 -- excuse me, just a moment. Page 8 where General Dragan Ilic is referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It's the ninth page in English version or -- it starts on the ninth page and continues to tenth page, and I think that we need the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a completely different topic now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you for another clarification. What page is it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is an eight-digit figure at the top of the page, the last three being 269.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that General Dragan Ilic addressed the meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is General Dragan Ilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: The chief of the crime police administration during the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see the first bullet point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: A meeting was referred to at which I was present as well as the other chiefs of OKPs in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is said here is that precise tasks and instructions were issued on how the crime investigation police should work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: That is what was indeed done then and it had to do with the necessities that cropped up in view of the state of war and also the fact that the situation became more complicated in terms of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at bullet point 7, that is on page 10, I think, in the English version. [In English] The fourth paragraph or dash on that page. [Interpretation] What it says here, a plan was made to take care of the territory that was distributed to all the departments of the crime police and the secretariats of the interior, and it specifies and defines clear tasks. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: specific activity in the terrain, that is to say to get a maximum out of it as far as crime is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court Exhibit 6D874.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have the document before you, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: 6D874, that's what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of a document is this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: These are the specific activities that are clearly spelled out in paragraphs and that pertain to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is written here? Who compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, what is written here is that it's the head of the staff, Major-General Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time did you know who it was that had compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Absolutely. I've said that. Dragan Ilic with two other men from the crime police department -- their orders were conveyed to us, "nalog," and that is indeed what they did, the way I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this -- actually, would you please look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the last sentence before the signature --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not find this and we could not follow the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not understanding the interpreter's difficulty. Is there not access to e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, there is but it was not on e-court at the time when the witness was speaking, the witness was reading from the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of this document, as is written at the very

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: as for these bullet points containing the measures, actions, and orders, the seven of them, my plan also contains who it is that was supposed to carry this out, that is to say I'm dealing with the human resources that will be used in order to carry this through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you remind us how it is you know that this is a document conveying the orders of Ilic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me this question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Another thing is possible too, that in such things there is an obligation that crops up for us vis-a-vis the staff to send reports. So that may have been the reason why this was done. I really cannot go into it any further in terms of providing an explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you work in the police, again I am going to persist even more than His Honour Judge Bonomy because I see that there is an issue that arose that we perhaps did not give thought to. Could Dragan Ilic from Pristina, or rather, send from Pristina this plan or this document and write UKP there, the unit that he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: He could, but that would involve an unnecessary loss of time, he did this for some practical reasons. There was no need for him to send it up there and since it pertains to the territory of Kosovo he did a practical thing, he used the address of the staff and he sent this to us through the staff. That is my understanding of the matter. As for the essence of his decision, I cannot go into that, or rather, my understanding of your question is why he did it that way and I really cannot say. I think that the reasons were of economy, to do it as practically as possible. I don't think that there was any ill intent involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that this dispatch has a number, 12A, strictly confidential number 21, this document, rather, not dispatch, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Just now up here I saw CALEO6, that is the nickname of the chief of the crime technical department of the MUP, so this links the document up to Mr. Ilic and Mr. Aleksic, who was with him at the time so I see the number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If a document is being sent from the staff by Dragan Ilic, can one put here a number or the number of the UKP or does it have to -- does it have to contain the number of the staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: When teleprinter people work or the support services of the staff, the telegraph people, then they use their own records and, quite simply, they register this regardless of who brings this -- well, I'm dealing with a hypothesis now, but it is possible that what I am claiming is that these are the positions of Dragan Ilic and he told us that we would receive this, it was sent from the teleprinter hall as a document and the people down there on Sreten's behalf sent this to the SUPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have an untranslated document. We will have to ask the honourable Trial Chamber whether they will allow us to use it. It is a sequel to the other two documents, it is 6D1634, and that is a document that we received a few days ago, two or three days ago, by fax and it is the witness who compiled this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You appear to be pushing at an open door, Mr. Lukic, there's no objection being taken, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- it will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's the date?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please read slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the basis of this document, the document that you have before you, 6D874?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes. That is precisely the way in which one is supposed to act when receiving such orders, "nalog."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: This is an operative plan, that is what I could call it. Here it is just called a plan of concrete activities in curbing and eliminating security negative occurrences of threatening the personal and property-related safety of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document is rather long.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It was adopted at the level of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just in order to speed up could we see paragraph 7, please. Could you please read it out to us because the document has not been translated. Just do it slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I'll be careful. "With inspection organs the local administration and public enterprises, establish direct and expedient cooperation in order to prevent all forms of unlawful conduct dealing with consequences of war operations, especially with regard to facilities that had been damaged, preparing and clearing roads, and normalising conditions of life and work. Within this task, pay particular attention to repairing facilities that were damaged and that are about to fall. Clear roads where war operations cause damage or presented obstacles as well as viewing and registering all the damage incurred that are a result of war operations. Within the normalisation of work and living conditions, view all aspects of supplies and problems that affect the resolving of these problems."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you in your work use the term "asanacija," clearing up of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here I see that you used the word "saniranje," or repair or restoring. Is this the usual term used by the police and why did you use it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I don't know we use it -- why I used it, it was adequate to the situation, to the measures and jobs that we had to do, and it was used in that form and for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this, or rather, at this meeting on the 5th of May, 1999, what was explained to you? What did clearing up or this "saniranje," what was it to encompass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: When a general holds a meeting, Dragan Ilic, because to me he was not only the greatest authority in the administration of the criminal police, we of course always kept minutes. This was just translated, replicated, from those minutes of that meeting into the "nalog" that we received, and we could not go beyond that in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. These were all the questions we had for you at this moment. Our colleagues from the Prosecution -- our colleagues from the Defence team will be asking you questions and then our colleagues from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I am Tomislav Visnjic, appearing for General Ojdanic, and I shall ask you a few questions associated mainly with paragraph 66 of your statement. Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up on e-court Exhibit P5138 -- 5138 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Until it is called up I shall asking you directly, are you insinuating or claiming in your statement or do you have any information to the effect that the army was involved in the hauling away of bodies from the firing range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P138 is the exhibit number. Thank you. Can we zoom in this part which says "firing range."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Visnjic was: "Are you claiming or insinuating in your statement that the army was involved in the hauling away of bodies from the firing range." Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly, Your Honour, in association with paragraph 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Witness, we have before us a section of a map showing the Prizren-Suva Reka road. Would you agree with me when I say that the section which encompasses the area called firing range was, in fact, the area between the Suva Reka-Prizren road and the roads leading from the Suva Reka-Prizren road to the villages of Ljubizda and Korisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to mark on the map this particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could get assistance from the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to warn you, however, that I'm not familiar with topography and such details so my markings will be of a police nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Well, follow these roads as I indicated them in that case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: The question of the map is also a problem that I am facing but I will do my very best.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The section of the Suva Reka-Prizren road which would include the area which is the border of the firing range.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: There is an arrow here which actually coincides with that. At that firing range I believe that the position of this most salient, highest feature was here because in the hinterland of the firing range there is this elevation, this hill, which was actually a protection barrier when firing was being executed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel and witness please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Please mark this entire area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It is much narrower than what I have indicated now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Do you agree when I say that, or rather, let me first ask you were you ever at this firing range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the area which includes the firing range is, in fact, not enclosed, it's not fenced off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that this area in fact is a flat land, a meadow, which is bounded on the one side by this Suva Reka-Prizren road and on the other side by this elevation which is a natural barrier in the firing range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: No, I cannot agree with you there. Would you like me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: No, this is actually a developed firing range where communicating trenches and breast work has been already made, military people can correct me if I'm wrong in any of these expressions, and from the very beginning in this section there was a miniature proving ground for the training of soldiers and there was a dirt road leading towards the firing range which was also developed that road, it was not a meadow to me, it was something that had been actually arranged beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that a lot of this firing range can, in fact, be seen from the Suva Reka-Prizren road from the road leading to Korisa and the one leading to Ljubizda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I remember well a section, a part, can be seen, there is a line of trees, walnut trees, which are quite high. And a part of the firing range of the grounds can be seen, but the firing range in its entirety cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with me that there were no features on the range except for a small house or 2 or 3 square metres which was some sort of a shelter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I did not mention this shed, but now I do remember it. I only mentioned the makeshift barriers which were there for the purpose of training, I presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Please take a look at Exhibit P120, page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, do you want an IC number for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. It slipped my mind.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit P120, page 2, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Witness, does this actually correspond to what you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Well, yes, more or less but the trees have probably been felled in the meantime and the roads shown here do not ring a bell. This creek here, however, does and I remember it well. Yes, yes, and these are the walnut trees that have been cut down. This road here to the left leads to the main road, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the date of this aerial photograph, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a Prosecution exhibit, Your Honour. I believe this was taken sometime in the year 2000 or perhaps a bit later, and I was there some two years after that and I found a similar situation in the terrain. So I believe it is 2002 or 2003 at the latest.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We're checking, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It appears to be 21 August 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is it, Witness, you say the walnut trees have been cut down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were here where there is this mound or heap of earth or sand or something. There was a line of trees there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I remember it more or less --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you use your pen there, please, and mark on it where the trees were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this extension of the road which I do not remember, shall I mark that too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is this section here, whereas I do remember this part but conditionally if that is the section leading towards the main road, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is to the very best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So please mark with a 1 the part of the road which you think leads to the main road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, I have -- I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with a number 2 the line that you believe used to be the line of trees before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And 3 is the number you will use to mark the part of the road which you do not remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Coming to the firing range was restricted so I was there only once when there was a drill practice, when there was firing practice, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time when there was no firing the firing range was quite free and there were no units or guards there, it was a wholly open area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I believe you, but I didn't even have the need to go to that firing range at that time and I have no experiences to share with you in that regard, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that during the war, throughout the war, the firing range was not operational, it was not used, nor were there any units, military units, stationed at it or at -- in its vicinity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I believe that it was so. I passed by the main road. I didn't notice any movements or any developments that would induce me to think otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what you have said now, can I take it that this part of your statement in paragraph 66, which refers to the statement for the police in Prizren, this could be an area that we could enter only upon consent of the authorisation by the military organs and the policemen could not know what was happening at the military firing range only refers to the period when there was firing at this feature, in this area, and when there were security guards there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I should like to respond a bit differently to -- or rephrase your question. Namely, in my answer policemen could go there only after the execution of firing had been already planned. After that we would receive authorisation from the military commanding officer that we could go there on a certain day, and it was only then that the police would go there for firing practice at that firing range. This is the way I understood it and I believe that -- so that most of the policemen that this was property of the Army of Yugoslavia, that it had a drilling -- sorry, firing practice equipment there and that it was under the control of the military commanding officers, the military organs, who were the ones issuing us permits or authorisations to go for firing practice there. That is the way I understood it and I did not change that view in respect of the war time-period because I believe that during the war time-period no one actually was at the firing range, not the police and not the army, at least that is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that in fact you don't know, you cannot assert that during the war one needed authorisation from the military organs to enter a facility where there was nothing and where there was nobody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Let me explain it in this way. Had I -- if I had had the need, had I needed to go there I would have reported or -- that to the military organ in charge. That is my response.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And that is your perception of how things stood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that completes my examination and I should like this second exhibit to be given an IC number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The second document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, for about ten minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe 20 minutes. I don't know yet, I have to check one more time my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's going to be your position, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can begin and take the rest of the day and probably go into tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, we have to break at this stage, that will be for an hour. While we have the break would you please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you again at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, you're back on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just for the transcript, IC193, IC192, they can be filed as public documents. We discussed it during the break, and I don't think that anyone's opposed to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court 6D1613.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: With regard to this document you've already had a discussion with

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I did not discuss this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: with Mr. Lukic. Since the document has not been translated, I would like to ask you to read the first paragraph after the heading "plan," et cetera. So would you please slowly read the first paragraph so that the interpreters can translate it for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: "With a view to cutting off and eliminating all negative security trends and the efficient prevention of the commission uncovering and capturing of perpetrators of the most serious crimes, especially murder, rape, different forms of abuse, theft, and aggravated theft, arson, and other damage done to private and state property, different forms of speculation and abuse as well as certain overstepping of authority, please take the following ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Could you please now read paragraph 3 so that we can have that translated as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just scroll down so we can see paragraph 3 and could the witness read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Please read out that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: "Establish direct contact with the organs of the Army of Yugoslavia, or rather, officers that are in charge of units deployed in the area and identify the presence of units both in terms of time as well as space in certain areas of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is your document dated the 8th of May as you've already said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: referring to number 12A, strictly confidential 21, and the date is the 6th of May, 1999; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I confirm that yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please call up in e-court P2159. Are you familiar with this document? Could we please zoom out the Serbian version so that the witness can see it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that the number of this document is 12A, number 20, and that the date is the same like the previous document, the 6th of May, 1999; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: You're right on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Since we do have a translation of this document, I kindly ask you to read to yourself the second paragraph of this document and then I'm going to put another question to you in relation to this. Just read it to yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 2 in English so that we can see this particular paragraph, paragraph number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: As far as the uncovering of crimes is concerned, there is a certain uniformity and there is a certain similarity involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: So you will agree with me that practically similar tasks are being issued in all three documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Well, just a moment. This is a different question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: All right. I'll rephrase. Is -- does it have to do with the same scope of work on the part of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 6D-2, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm Djuro Cepic, and I appear for General Lazarevic. I have a few questions for you, so could you please take your statement. First I'd like to deal with paragraph 42 of your statement. You said there

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: peace and that the only difference involved the shifts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned that but since you're mentioning it that requires a complex number of issues to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have no other questions in relation to this. Other state institutions - I'm referring to courts, prosecutor's offices, municipalities - did they function practically in the same way in wartime as they did in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: In peacetime and later on in wartime, if I can put it that way. The public prosecutor's office and the district court had their own duty services, and the municipality during the war did have, I do remember that, bit of an active role, a bit more active and some kind of work that can be referred to in those terms as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 50 you describe the suffering of civilians in Korisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether the members of the Army of Yugoslavia came to the aid of the citizens who were the victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any knowledge to the effect that the members of the army in some other situations as well came to the aid of civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you just mention one or two such situations, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It primarily had to do with people who were seeking shelter in 1998 when the police and the army provided them with food, medical assistance, and the rest. I also remember these people who were seeking shelter in a mountain to the left of Orahovac, I cannot remember exactly but that was one such case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 57 of your statement, you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You refer to Srbica here. You will agree with me that it's a mistake, you meant Orahovac, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: You said 57?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 57, the events referred to, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I cannot make any amendments now. You're probably right. Let me read the text. I think you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you refer to some documents here of the 549th Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you go on to that, why do you say that, Mr. Cepic, because 72(c) is Srbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, in the lower part of the text what is stated there, namely, what the witness is referring to, P1995, and the other documents of the 549th Brigade, they have to do with the area of Orahovac not Srbica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very hard to deal with such a complex set of events in one paragraph only. One would have to consult the indictment and see whether it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, can you identify the paragraph to which it appears to be a reference if it's the wrong number?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, my assistant --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I require the assistance of my assistant. Could I just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honour, 72(a), Orahovac, that's what the indictment says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, do you have a B/C/S copy of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, no, I have it in English on my assistant's screen. My colleague Mr. Fila has been of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you show to the witness paragraph 72(a).

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It can't be that paragraph because it doesn't -- what he says in paragraph 57 doesn't bear resemblance to the facts there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, I just wanted to put one question to make a distinction between the first and second part of the paragraph since I may have misunderstood the way it is phrased here. The second sentence of the photograph says that the witness knew of the actions that took place in the area, and then there is a reference made of the document of the 549th Brigade which mentions Orahovac rather than Srbica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can see the sequence of paragraph references, we've had 72(a), (b), there's a mistake in paragraph 55, that's been sorted out, and then we go to (c). So you've completed what you have to ask on that, have you? Well, it will have to be dealt with in re-examination or that paragraph will have to be deleted from the statement, but you continue now with your own cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can take that document -- the witness has it. Well, he should retain it just now and he may be asked questions about it later. Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Witness, these documents of the 549th Brigade mentioned in the paragraph, you saw those for the first time quite much later after the war. Is it the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: That is why I said that I was familiar, meaning that I learned about it subsequently, that's how I would explain it from my point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 60 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Here you mention the work you carried out in Pusto Selo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Paragraph 60?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How do you call those activities in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we call it exhumation or something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Exhumation, but it's not a police term, it's a term used by the judge. It's not exclusively a police term.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: However, you were in the field following the judge's order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, we exhumed the bodies of the victims that we found there, they had been buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: And I mentioned here that had we come across such a thing in Bela Crkva we would have done the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just one detail concerning Bela Crkva, the same paragraph, the 17th of April, 1999. It says there was reason to believe or to doubt that after the terrorist action in the Kelmendi house two corpses were found. I reviewed the document and I can see that in the document it says after an anti-terrorist action on the part of the Army of Yugoslavia. I did some additional research and reviewed a number of documents. I can say with certainty that in April there was no VJ unit that was included in any anti-terrorist actions in the area of Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if that's a -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If that's a question from Mr. Cepic, it should be in the form of a question rather than a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, I was about to put my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, you will allow for a possibility that wrong information was entered in relation to what I have just stated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I can allow for such a possibility, but I put more trust in what is stated in the document. I suggest that we consult the original file. I think the operative who wrote that had reason to put it there. I have no reason to doubt his conduct. Consulting the file could do away with the doubt you have, it would either turn out to be that it was a mistake or you would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Visnjic asked you a number of questions about the firing range in Ljubizda. It was a temporary firing range, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: My experience prompts me to tell you that it was a military firing range. As for whether it was temporary or permanent, I don't know, I can't say either way. You are probably more familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the vicinity of that area was there a police station in Ljubizda or a control -- or a check-point manned by the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: During what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: April, March, the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: There is a building, there is a police squad in Ljubizda between the firing range and the town, closer to the town itself, along the main road. During the war --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: That is correct, but since I was tasked with dealing with crime I could use that building and I had cooperation with the uniformed part of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I could go back to the document which is 6D614 in e-court. I wanted to draw your attention to the part referring to identified perpetrators and measures taken against army members. The same title is found in two sections of the document. What is mentioned there are volunteers and a volunteer unit. You will agree with me that in the area of KiM, in your experience, you didn't come across volunteer units, rather, there were individual volunteers which were made part of certain units in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I would agree with that. What is not clear to me here is how this title was made based on what. I'm not familiar with the existence of any volunteer units.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I also came across a number of criminal complaints against unidentified perpetrators in this document. You will agree with me that any further work in shedding light on the aforementioned --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Cepic please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the approach were set about working at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the needs of the transcript, I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I came across quite a number of criminal reports or complaints submitted against unidentified perpetrators. You will agree with me that any further work in shedding light on the aforementioned events was carried out by the military and civilian judiciary as well as prosecution organs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: The forwarding of that material was supposed to result in that and they set about that job in a proper manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you come across any members of the civilian defence in

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would I be right if I said that they wore the old type of uniform that used to be worn by the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, those were the uniforms that could be seen in the old partisan movies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'd call them M-77 but I suppose it doesn't mean much to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I suppose you also have knowledge of the abuse of military uniforms which had previously been issued to members of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: As part of my work I also have operational information at my disposal. It pointed to the fact that during the 1990s a number of uniforms stayed with various persons and civilians. We had that in mind, particularly when we were trying to work on the perpetrators of crimes who wore such uniforms. There was abuse of that uniform, and as the crime police we had to bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Reviewing the document I found out that some cases were forwarded to the military judiciary, whereas others were sent to civilian courts. Were there any cases in which any further work on the individual cases be carried out by the military security organs and that the perpetrators were processed in -- before civilian courts because they no longer enjoyed the status of military personnel by that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Such a possibility did exist and I will need some time to clear that up. After a number of VJ members had been kidnapped, I think there was a transport of soldiers to Nis because they committed misdemeanours and thefts, and they were kidnapped by the KLA along the route. To speed up the proceedings, although I don't have specific data now, that could be clarified, checked, the military organs disarmed and disengaged the reserve soldier, turned him into a civilian, so that that particular perpetrator could be processed before a civilian court. That was the reason there was no attempt at manipulation. I think there was an agreement between the courts, but that's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You mentioned some kidnapped soldiers. Do you know anything more about their fate?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what information you gained. I have a photograph in the system, it is 5D13 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Forget it, Mr. Cepic. Let's proceed with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell us what information you obtained in the further investigation of this matter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: You are referring to my role and what I knew given the fact that I only worked there for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I managed to assist the team in question, and with great efforts to explain to them that the photograph, that one of those photographs most probably came from the territory of Albania. And I explained because of the -- of the growth, the vegetation which was in the background of the persons. Across the Junik mountains the climate is a Mediterranean one and the growth there is usually like that on the photograph. We have a different climate in the territory of Serbia, we have a continental climate and a different kind of vegetation. So this was the conclusion we drew and we identified some of the sufferers in question and we also obtained the name of one of the possible perpetrators. Thereafter I was assigned to different missions and other missions and other people continued that particular job. Is this enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That will suffice. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, what was your point to be about that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I objected to the photograph several times in the past. I don't know what probative value it has, it's being offered for shock value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now we have a possible probative value set out in the answer that the witness has given.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the relevance of this evidence is, to some argumented issue in the case. I'm not sure what it pertains to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the issue that this pertains to, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is at the critical period which is covered by the indictment, this event from April 1999 namely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would appear, though, that it occurred in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these persons that witness just spoke about were kidnapped on the Prizren-Suva Reka road and there are minutes, records, of that, and this is contained -- there was a criminal complaint filed and this is in the document 5D962. These people were actually prosecuted, people from the 549th Brigade. And if you will allow me, both Colonel Delic and Colonel Mitic spoke about this critical event, and of course this witness gave us more information about it. And I suppose that the witness has more extensive information about it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've caused me more confusion. Who was prosecuted for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I give you the answer? I believe that the kidnapped soldiers, the kidnapped soldiers were being escorted because of the criminal offences perpetrated to the military court in Nis and in the Crnoljevo gorge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Cepic, you say that people from the 549th Brigade were prosecuted for this. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically the people who were kidnapped for some other crimes, for theft, they were being escorted, but the same document, if you will allow me, also cites a criminal complaint against unidentified perpetrators who are members of the 549th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what were they accused of?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theft. Soldiers are accused of theft, and the other crime is that of kidnapping by the NN, unidentified perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's move on then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 6D-2, you established the authenticity of the photograph in the procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: The photograph is authentic. I only said that it showed the consequence, where the actual decapitation took place is not shown by the photograph. The photograph is just evidence that it was, indeed, done. The photographs are authentic and that was accepted by UNMIK, too. UNMIK police found them when searching the area around Pec. This is the information that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the Prosecutor has no objection I should like to ask that these photographs be tendered, they be admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Of course I have an objection, Your Honour, this is not relevant to any contested issue in the case, and I haven't heard a foundation establishing how he determined that those were authentic other than saying that they were. I don't know which ones he looked at. This is a wild goose chase, and it should be stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the issue that these will assist us with, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I understood the indictment refers to an armed conflict in the area of Kosmet in the matter covered by the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you deny that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot state an opinion on such an important issue, but this photograph does corroborate that there was a serious armed conflict between the KLA and the forces of the army and the police of Serbia on the other side. It corroborates that it was a very serious armed conflict between two warring parties, and it also substantiates another fact, I shall be free to say, that is one about the conduct of an organization and the activities of an organization, which called itself the KLA but which many circles have called a terrorist organization. In my humble opinion the photographs of this witness corroborate precisely that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was or was not an armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot really say with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You must have a point of view by now, Mr. Cepic, on whether there was an armed conflict in April of 1999 or not surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I can see from the file, it refers to terrorist actions of the KLA on the one side and the anti-terrorist actions of the forces of Serbia and Yugoslavia on the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's plain from the answers given by the witness and also by the position taken by Mr. Cepic that the photographs would add nothing to our knowledge on the question of whether or not there was an armed conflict in the area that we're concerned with which is Kosovo. So we will not admit these photographs. Please proceed, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. 6D-2, thank you very much. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why did you not write to him and ask if he could assist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no such authority. I was not in such a position as to be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You cannot ask a senior officer for guidance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can ask for guidance and for other things, but I had no occasion to do anything of that sort with General Obradovic [as interpreted]. Because the services had talked about it with him to the best of my information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we're not to be given an explanation of why there are no PJP reports available?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you expected one from me, this is all that I can say at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I just want to follow-up on a couple

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you be willing to do that for us and send it in after you go back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I shall do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- not to me. So please pursue it, Mr. Hannis. It's just a vague cloud at the moment to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's not clear to me either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's ask it again and see where you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which colleague? We're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I think that it was my colleague Obrad, his first name was also Obrad, I don't remember his last name. I think that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You don't remember his last name? How long did he work with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I'll try to remember. He didn't actually work with me, he was in that sector working for Mr. Furdulovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In that section working with Mr. Furdulovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember his last name but there is just one Obrad there and you can easily identify him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, what was it that led you to believe that he was doing everything in his power. I had the impression that you didn't really know what he was doing in that regard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It's possible that you are right, but based on that one conversation that was something that I heard quite by chance, I concluded that that presented a serious problem for them and that's the only thing on the basis of which I believe that that's the role that he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I had no authority to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Why not? Are they in a higher standing than SUP chiefs? They're not, are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: They don't belong to the chief of the SUP, these PJP detachments, that's the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what was the problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you explain your question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You called it a problem, and I would like to know what the problem was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem was because it was my understanding that those reports had gone missing, that they existed and then they went missing, that's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And did you think this was a cover up of some kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have enough facts to support it, but one could give that interpretation as well, that somebody put that away, put that away somewhere and that they're now gone from that section. That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before the Judge asked you a couple questions there I think you had said something about reports about PJP activity were in the MUP daily reports, you mean MUP staff daily reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Those were the daily reports, the daily overviews, somebody calls them reports but you could also call them a daily bulletin or overview. "Pregled" is the Serbian word.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we're talking about the same thing I think this is something that was sometimes also called a bulletin or an overview or a summary of security-related events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Bulletin would be the most appropriate word.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was this a report that went from MUP staff to the ministry, is that the one you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: To organizational units within the seat of the MUP and return information was also sent to all SUPs, if I remember that well. If we had one here before us I could explain it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I think we might have one. Let me pull that up now, it's sort of out of order. Could we look at P1693. I think this is from the 1st of May, 1999, and I think this may be what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you seen this particular one before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now -- so this is the report you were talking about. Is it your evidence that the actions of the PJP were reported in these daily bulletins?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Could I leaf through this document? Could I see the following pages of this bulletin and then I could give you a more reliable answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I'll look and see if I have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: The entire document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do. With the help of the usher I'll hand you a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It's not in this bulletin. As was stated in another file, that after an anti-terrorist action of the army, two bodies were found of persons who had been killed. In certain reports there should be information whenever we are reporting on anything there should be information on the cause and what preceded a particular crime. So there you can find a link between actions and consequences. It must be a mistake or perhaps I saw it in another bulletin. It is not contained in this particular one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And now you see on the first page this has a number, 10-121/2. Can you tell us anything about the numbering system in connection with the MUP staff and these daily surveys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: There is an instruction in existence. Without it I cannot tell you anything in particular about the numbering system of the MUP and on assigning certain designators and numbers to certain organizational units. It is at the level of the whole ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: And it is not a part of my domain, my field of work. I'd rather not go into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well let me ask you this: It's my understanding that the first number usually referred to some organization within the MUP. Is that right, the number 10?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: There is that possibility but I'm speculating. This number -- I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm going on --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm going on more what I learned of looking at VJ documents, but after the dash then the next number would be a sequential number for --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: There is a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But the next number would be a sequential number during the year. So the next number, 121, would be the 121st document related to whatever number 10 was for the year. Do you follow me so far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I am following. However, our way of marking documents - and I can tell you that at a greater degree of certainty although I'm not fully competent - is not something you can compare with the numbering system of the Army of Yugoslavia. I'm not very well-versed in this field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, this is a daily report for the 1st of May, 1999, and I suggest to you that the 1st of May, 1999, is right about the 121st day of the year in 1999, right? 31 days in January, 28 in February, 31 in March, 30 in April. The 1st of May would be about 121, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I understand you fully and I accept your explanation. There is logic to it. However, if we want to be precise we would have to consult the instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And these were daily reports, and we see this one is for the time-period from 0600 on the 30th of April to the 0600 on the 1st of May, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: These are daily reviews of -- I keep hearing "reports" in the interpretation I'm receiving.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: They resemble a bulletin rather than a type of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll accept your terminology. I don't have a problem with that. The topics covered in this particular bulletin, number 1, were attacks by NATO; number 2 were terror attacks, which I take it would be the KLA; number 3 are serious crimes committed; number 4 in this one is persons who fled the territory. And could you have a look at that for a second while we've got this document open.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: You mean the last page, number 5 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Number 4 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: -- concerning the persons who left -- number 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- persons who left. I see it says between 24 April and 30 April 1999, a total of 715.158 persons belonging to the Siptar national minority left the territory. You were aware, weren't you, that from the start of the NATO bombing until the 1st of May, hundreds of thousands of Siptars had left the territory, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I'm afraid I have to correct you a bit. It wasn't only Siptars who were leaving the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, my question was about this. This says 715.000 Siptars. You were aware that hundreds of thousands of them had left by then, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: The word "Siptars" is a bit misplaced, I think. It was the Albanian minority and this may have been a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: A mistake by General Lukic or whoever wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: I am afraid that this report was not authorised. I accepted the way you put it to me. If I saw General Lukic's signature, I would be able to tell you that it was a mistake on his part.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I have a question about that. This document doesn't have a signature. Is that normal for this kind of document in the MUP in 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: It is not normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, can you explain that for me then because some of the documents that you were shown on direct I think do not have a signature of General Lukic, there's just a typewritten title and name, right? We can look at those again in a minute, but do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 6D-2
utterances.text: This is a Telex message. It had its designators which may assist in ascertaining its authenticity if that's what you mean. There are two documents in question here and I attended the first one of the two, meetings referred to. I had additional information and I could confirm what is in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand the point you're making about the Telex or the telegram, but let me take you to a couple others that you looked at before. First one is 6D666 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
